facts.fact_text: On 22 April 2000, the applicant organised a demonstration in Sultanahmet Square in Istanbul.
The demonstration organised by the applicant on 22 April 2000 took the form of a march followed by a statement to the press.
The demonstration organised by the applicant on 22 April 2000 was held to protest against plans for 'F-type' prisons.
The police asked the group gathered in Sultanahmet Square to disperse and to end the gathering.
The police informed the group via a loudspeaker that the demonstration was unlawful because advance notice had not been submitted.
The police informed the group via a loudspeaker that the demonstration was likely to cause public-order problems at a busy time of day.
The demonstrators refused to obey the police order to disperse.
The demonstrators attempted to continue marching towards the police.
The police dispersed the group of demonstrators using a kind of tear gas known as 'pepper spray'.
The police arrested thirty-nine demonstrators, including the applicant.
Article 34 of the Turkish Constitution provides that everyone has the right to hold unarmed and peaceful meetings and demonstration marches without prior permission.

Article 34 of the Turkish Constitution provides that the formalities, conditions, and procedures governing the exercise of the right to hold meetings and demonstration marches shall be prescribed by law.

At the material time, section 10 of Law no. 2911 on assemblies and marches required that, in order for a meeting to take place, the governor's office or authorities of the district in which the demonstration is planned must be informed during opening hours and at least seventy-two hours prior to the meeting.
Under section 10 of Law no. 2911 on assemblies and marches, the required notice must contain the signature of all the members of the organising board.
The police informed the group via a loudspeaker that the demonstration was likely to cause public-order problems at a busy time of day.

Section 24 of Law no. 2911 on assemblies and marches provides that demonstrations and processions which do not comply with the provisions of that Act will be dispersed by force on the order of the governor's office and after the demonstrators have been warned.

The police arrested thirty-nine demonstrators, including the applicant.
After an identity check, the applicant was released at 12.45 p.m. on 22 April 2000.
